On Sun, Aug 9, 2026 at 9:12 AM Jane Holloway <jane.holloway@stratagem.com> wrote:
> Diego,
> We're seeing a high rate of 500 responses...

Thanks for the logs, Jane — useful samples. Triage notes below (high level):
- Symptom: serialization mismatch at the request boundary. Stratagem's gateway is sending `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-16` on a subset of messages. Our current tokenizer path expects utf-8; the utf-16 payloads trigger a decode failure in the attention packing code and bubble up as 500.
- Root cause (probable): a middleware version in Stratagem's deployment that started sending utf-16 on a feature flag.
- Quick mitigation (recommended): enable the fallback routing Diego mentioned — route to quantized-v2 model variant which uses the older stable tokenizer path (no attention kernel mismatch). This is a safe short-term move and reversible.
- Longer-term fix: either force UTF-8 normalization at the gateway or add a robust decode guard in the runtime. We'll ship the decode-guard in the next hotfix if you prefer.

Proposed canary plan (attached: redwood_canary_plan_0809.pdf):
1) Approve fallback route now.
2) Roll to 10% of traffic for 15 minutes, monitor error rate and latency.
3) If stable, ramp to 100% for next 2 hours while we coordinate a permanent fix.

SLA ask: given production impact, Stratagem is eligible for an accelerated P1 engagement window. We propose updating the partner escalation SLA to require 1-hour response for P1 incidents during business hours and a written acknowledgement within 4 hours for off-hours P1s. I attached a short proposed amendment (proposed-sla-amendment-stratagem.pdf). If legal/finance are in agreement we can fast-track a DocuSign addendum.

I can host the bridge at 11:30 PDT (we have the SREs and runtime engineers standing by).

Marissa Cole
